subject: HelioHealth: Request for latency remedy & contract term exemption
messages:
From: Samantha Liao <samantha@heliohealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency thresholds + remedy ask (HelioHealth)

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our engineers are excited about the integration. A quick heads up from our infra team: HelioHealth requires a written commitment on 99.95% uptime for production endpoints in our US region and a 150ms 95th percentile latency target for internal-facing inference calls. Our legal team flagged Redwood's standard remedies (service credits capped at 5%) as insufficient for our risk profile.

We're not asking you to change your standard public terms lightly — this is tied to an RFP and an enterprise procurement review. Can Redwood provide: 1) an exception for the latency SLA to 150ms p95 and 2) an enhanced remedy schedule (tiered credits with a higher cap) for the first 12 months? We can share the RFP and compliance checklist (attached).

Attached: helio_health_requirements.pdf

Can you point me to who on your side owns exceptions like this? We anticipate a decision needed by EOD 6/12 to stay on our vendor short list.

Best,
Samantha
Infrastructure Program Manager
HelioHealth

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency thresholds + remedy ask (HelioHealth)

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding a request from HelioHealth (attached). Key asks: 150ms p95 latency in US, and a higher-tiered remedy schedule (they want larger credits for early-year outages). They need a written position by 6/12 EOD to remain in their short list.

Context / my read: HelioHealth is a strategic target in healthcare. The ask includes both a latency SLO exception (tighter p95) and a non-standard remedy cap. I recommend we:
- Offer a temporary 12-month exception that documents the 150ms p95 target for a defined traffic profile (internal inference only) with performance guardrails.
- Define a tiered credit schedule for the first 12 months (e.g., 10% cap first 6 months, 7.5% next 6 months) tied to incident review and remediation plan.
- Include an operational commitment: weekly health reports + a 2-week pilot to collect representative traces before go-live.

Attachments: redwood_proposed_remedy.xlsx (draft numbers)

Can one of you escalate to Deal Desk / Exec for approval? If useful I can prepare a short one-pager with impact to ARR and precedent examples.

Thanks,
Alex

On Thu, 4 Jun 2026 at 09:30, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Alex — copying Dylan for exec signoff and Tessa for legal coordination.
>
> TL;DR: Strategic account in healthcare requesting a p95 latency exception (150ms) and higher initial remedy caps. We can accept temporarily with controls, but this requires exec approval due to modified remedy caps and precedent risk.
>
> Recommendation (deal desk):
> - Approve a 12-month exception to document 150ms p95 for the specified internal inference routes only, contingent on a 2-week pilot and 24/7 escalation channel during the first 60 days.
> - Remedy schedule (first 12 months only):
>   * Severity 1 cumulative downtime > 1.5% in a month: 10% service credit (cap for month)
>   * Severity 1 cumulative downtime > 3% in a month: 20% service credit
>   * Overall annual cap for credits during the 12-month period: 12% of monthly recurring charges
> - Offer a 5% one-time discount on committed monthly spend as commercial concession in lieu of a higher ongoing cap.
>
> Impact note: This raises our exposure slightly vs. standard terms but will likely secure a multi-year expansion opportunity. See attached financial impact calc.
>
> Request to Dylan: please confirm executive approval to proceed with the exception and the concession above. If approved, I will draft an addendum for HelioHealth and route to Legal/Contracts.
>
> Regards,
> Marissa
> VP, Enterprise Sales
> Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: HelioHealth: Request for latency remedy & contract term exemption

Thanks for the summary, Marissa. I reviewed the recommendation and the financials. Approve the 12-month exception under the following conditions:

1) The 150ms p95 commitment is documented narrowly (internal inference endpoints only) and limited to the US region; any expansion to external/public endpoints requires a separate review.
2) Remedy caps and the 5% one-time concession are acceptable, but Legal must include a rollback clause if incident post-mortems indicate systemic regressions.
3) Require the 2-week pilot and a post-pilot performance validation report before enabling production traffic.
4) Deal Desk should capture an explicit executive approval note in the deal record and obtain confirmation from Procurement on SLA acceptance.

Marissa — if you can route the draft addendum to Legal and Contracts with the clauses above, proceed. Alex — coordinate the pilot and provide sample traces to HelioHealth next week. Rishi — please stand ready for onboarding and ensure our SREs are on the rotation for the first 60 days.

Dylan
SVP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
